issues.body:
AGENTS.md:7 lands the rule: "Model-qualified header markers such as `[OPUS-5]`, `[FABLE-5]`, and `[HAIKU-…]` are legacy and migrate when touched."

Read as "when the FILE is touched", this PR is non-compliant with the rule it introduces: it edits scripts/policy-resolve.py while leaving 8 legacy markers in that file, and edits policy/repos.toml while leaving 6. Read as "when that HEADER line is rewritten" — which is what the diff actually does — the PR is compliant and the residual markers are documented backlog.

I re-measured the blast radius this round: 178 legacy `[OPUS-5]`/`[FABLE-5]`/`[HAIKU-…]` markers across 43 files. Under the file reading, any future edit to scripts/dispatch-claim.py (35 markers) or select-and-claim.py (15) drags a large incidental header churn into an unrelated diff; under the header-line reading it drags none. A future reviewer citing this sentence has no text to settle which one they are enforcing.

Comment/prose only, nothing parses it, no trust check depends on it — not blocking, and it did not block in round 2 either. Re-raised only because the head is unchanged and the finding therefore still stands.
issues.fix_hint: Three words at AGENTS.md:7 make the unit explicit, e.g. "… are legacy; convert one when you edit that header line, not merely when you edit the file." Nothing else needs to change — the rest of the paragraph is accurate and mirrors .claude/agents/registry-docs.md:20, so the two will not drift.
issues.title: "migrate when touched" still does not say whether the unit of touch is the header line or the file (unchanged since round 2)

verdict.summary:
Round 3 head is unchanged from round 2 (no commit addressing round 2's nit), so my independent re-review reaches the same place: the change is correct and complete, and the single nit from round 2 survives verbatim.

What the diff is: ten one-line source-header swaps of the model-qualified marker `[GPT-5.6]` to the model-agnostic `[SPARQ agent]`, plus a 3-line paragraph in AGENTS.md that defines the convention. Every changed line is 1:1 (identical text after the marker) and sits ahead of `FROM`, the shebang/module docstring, or `set -euo pipefail`.

Checks I ran myself on the head tree (Read/Glob/Grep; Bash was denied by policy, so I could not run `git diff` and the FILE LIST rests on the harness-supplied diff — the CONTENT of each listed file I verified directly):
- Sweep complete: a tree-wide grep for the literal `[GPT-5.6]` returns ZERO matches, and exactly 11 `[SPARQ agent]` markers exist, matching the 10 header swaps plus AGENTS.md:6.
- Surviving plain-prose `GPT-5.6` mentions (README 84/250/262, orchestration/routing.toml 254/268, policy/repos.toml 5/10/16/23, triage.py:186, plan-alert.py:8, worker-live.sh model_display_name + its #97 literals) are the issue-#97 variant-qualified taxonomy and are correctly untouched; genericizing them would re-assert the mislabelling #97 exists to stop.
- No vacuous-test question arises: nothing executable changed, so no self-test is owed. I checked the seams that DO read these files and all are content/structure-addressed, not line-addressed: groom.py:10866 locates `  groom:` by `.index()`; worker-issue.py:2635 parses worker.yml through `worker_refusal_seam`; policy-resolve.py:1030 loads repos.toml via `tomllib` (a leading comment is inert); worker-live.sh's `_assert_dockerfile_pinned` reads `FROM ...@sha256:` which is unchanged. No consumer reads a `#` header line, and each header sentence occurs exactly once tree-wide, so no doc copy can diverge.
